# {{< meta course >}} · Day 4 {.course-day-slide}

Thursday, September 17, 2026

# Skill of the Day

::: {.big-prompt}
Describe
:::

Observe gives you information.

Describe lets you communicate it.

Participate lets you act with it.

# Describe It

1. One person receives an object or item.
2. Describe it without saying what it is.
3. Words only. No gestures.
4. The class shouts out guesses.
5. Take turns.

::: {.big-prompt}
Make us see it with your words.
:::

# What made a description useful?

- What details helped you guess?
- What happened when the description was vague?
- Which words communicated the most information?

# Why Describe?

- Description turns observation into communication.
- Technical work needs precise language.
- Describing forces you to notice details.
- Explaining something helps you learn it better.

# Technical Language

::: {.big-prompt}
Specific words reduce misunderstanding.
:::

Not:<br>
“that thing”

Better:<br>
“the red positive battery terminal”

# Technical Language

Not:<br>
“it is broken”

Better:<br>
“the wire insulation is cut”

# Describe to Learn

::: {.big-prompt}
When you describe what you know, you have to organize what you know.
:::

Teaching someone else is one way of learning more deeply.

# Observe → Describe → Participate

::: {.big-prompt}
Notice it.

Put it into words.

Do something with it.
:::

# When You Present

- Come up when your name is called.
- Use whatever you prepared.
- If it is incomplete, **present what you have**.

::: {.big-prompt}
You do not need to impress us.<br>
Help us know you. Help us connect with you.
:::

# While Others Present

For each presenter:

1. **Presenter**
2. **One thing I learned**
3. **A connection, something interesting, or something I want to remember**

**Short notes are enough.**

::: {.big-prompt}
The goal is to actually listen.
:::
